basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 25.' and it opens 'Vers. 25. Cognovit adhuc quoque Adam uxorem suam, et peperit filium vocavitque nomen ejus'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 25. Cognovit adhuc quoque Adam uxorem suam, et peperit filium vocavitque nomen ejus Seth. Seth positio interpretatur, quae Graece thesis dicitur, ducta etymologia ex eo quod pater dixit: posuit mihi Deus semen pro Abel. Alio sensu Seth resurrectio interpretatur, quia surrexit loco fratris sui interfecti.
